status: Reusable external patient-content definitions; clinical source hash freeze pending; not clinical approval
generic_chemotherapy_risks: Discuss low blood counts with serious infection or sepsis, anaemia and bleeding; nausea or vomiting; mouth soreness, appetite or taste changes, diarrhoea or constipation; fatigue, hair, nail and skin changes; changes in sexual wellbeing; allergic reactions and intravenous-line complications; blood clots, including clots in the legs or lungs; fertility, pregnancy and breastfeeding effects; and the possibility of lasting organ injury, later cancers or death from serious treatment complications. The likelihood and severity differ between medicines, doses and people. Read this general section together with the risks of every medicine actually included in the agreed treatment phase.
generic_urgent_advice: Follow the hospital's temperature and contact instructions. Contact oncology immediately for fever, shaking chills, suddenly feeling unwell, unusual bleeding, new breathlessness, very little urine, severe rash or vomiting that prevents drinking. Report pain, burning, swelling or leaking at an infusion site immediately. Severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse or seizures require emergency help. Drug-specific urgent advice below supplements this general plan.

doxorubicin.name: Doxorubicin
doxorubicin.mechanism: Damages genetic material and disrupts cell division
doxorubicin.explanation: Doxorubicin interferes with deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), the cell's genetic material, and the enzymes that manage it. Cancer cells can be damaged, but blood production, the mouth and the heart can also be affected. Previous anthracycline treatment contributes to the heart-risk assessment.
visual: Genetic material is damaged
Cell division is disrupted
Blood counts and heart function are checked
doxorubicin.watch: Report fever, new breathlessness, chest symptoms or palpitations urgently. Tell staff immediately about infusion-site burning or pain. Temporary red urine may reflect the medicine's colour, but visible blood, clots, painful urination or persistent red urine needs assessment.
risks: Low blood counts, serious infection or sepsis, anaemia and bleeding
Nausea, vomiting, mouth ulcers, appetite/bowel changes, hair loss and fatigue
Cumulative heart-muscle damage and heart failure, including effects that can appear after treatment; heart-rhythm disturbances
Severe tissue damage if the medicine leaks outside the vein; allergic reactions
Later blood cancers and potentially lasting fertility effects; pregnancy harm

ifosfamide.name: Ifosfamide
ifosfamide.mechanism: Links genetic strands so cells cannot divide normally
ifosfamide.explanation: The liver activates ifosfamide into substances that damage deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), the cell's genetic material. Some breakdown products can injure the urinary tract. Mesna and prescribed fluids reduce bladder injury, but do not remove kidney, brain or other chemotherapy risks.
visual: Activated medicine damages genetic material
Mesna helps protect the bladder
Brain, kidney, urine and blood checks continue
ifosfamide.watch: Report confusion, unusual sleepiness, hallucinations, marked weakness or seizures immediately. Blood or pain when passing urine, reduced urine, fever or new breathing problems needs urgent review. Continue prescribed mesna and hydration until the team confirms completion.
risks: Low blood counts, serious infection or sepsis, anaemia and bleeding
Nausea, vomiting, mouth/bowel effects, hair loss and fatigue
Brain effects causing confusion, drowsiness, hallucinations or seizures; recovery is not guaranteed
Bladder inflammation or bleeding, kidney filtering/tubular injury and electrolyte losses; kidney damage can persist or appear later
Serious heart or lung injury; allergic reactions
Potentially permanent infertility, later cancers and pregnancy harm

etoposide.name: Etoposide
etoposide.mechanism: Interferes with an enzyme that manages breaks in genetic material
etoposide.explanation: Etoposide interferes with topoisomerase II, an enzyme that manages breaks in deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), the cell's genetic material. Damaged cancer cells cannot divide normally. Blood production and other healthy tissues can also be affected.
visual: Genetic-material repair is disrupted
Dividing cells are damaged
Slow infusion and blood-count checks protect safety
etoposide.watch: Tell the nurse immediately about dizziness, flushing, rash, chest tightness, breathlessness, faintness or infusion-site pain. Contact oncology promptly for fever, bleeding, severe mouth symptoms or a blistering rash.
risks: Low blood counts, serious infection or sepsis, anaemia and bleeding
Nausea, vomiting, appetite loss, mouth soreness and bowel changes
Hair loss and fatigue
Allergic or severe infusion reactions and low blood pressure, particularly with rapid administration
Inflammation or tissue injury at the infusion site, liver effects and severe skin reactions
Later blood cancers, fertility effects and pregnancy harm

vincristine.name: Vincristine
vincristine.mechanism: Disrupts the structures needed for cell division
vincristine.explanation: Vincristine interferes with microtubules, structures needed for cells to divide and for nerves to work normally. This helps explain numbness, weakness and bowel slowing. It is given only into a vein by trained staff; administration into spinal fluid can be fatal.
visual: Microtubules are disrupted
Cell division and nerves are affected
Bowel and nerve symptoms need early review
vincristine.watch: Report new numbness, weakness, difficulty walking, jaw pain or hearing/vision changes before another dose. Constipation with pain, vomiting or abdominal swelling, difficulty passing urine, confusion or seizures needs urgent advice. Report infusion-site pain immediately.
risks: Peripheral nerve injury causing tingling, pain, weakness or impaired walking/hand function; effects may persist
Autonomic nerve injury causing severe constipation or bowel paralysis, urinary retention and blood-pressure changes
Low sodium from abnormal water retention, confusion or seizures; hearing, vision or cranial-nerve effects
Hair loss, mouth/bowel symptoms and jaw or muscle pain; blood-count effects can occur in the combination
Allergic reactions, breathing reactions and tissue injury after leakage outside the vein
Fertility and pregnancy harm; wrong-route administration can be fatal

cyclophosphamide.name: Cyclophosphamide
cyclophosphamide.mechanism: Damages genetic material after activation in the body
cyclophosphamide.explanation: Cyclophosphamide is activated into substances that damage deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), the cell's genetic material. Blood and reproductive cells can also be affected. Urinary breakdown products can injure the bladder, so the prescribed fluid and any mesna plan must be followed.
visual: Activated medicine damages genetic material
Urinary metabolites can irritate the bladder
Blood, urine and fluid checks support safety
cyclophosphamide.watch: Report blood or pain when passing urine, reduced urine, fever, new breathlessness, chest symptoms, confusion or severe weakness urgently. Follow the individual fluid plan; do not force large fluid volumes if you have a fluid restriction.
risks: Low blood counts, serious infection or sepsis, anaemia and bleeding
Bladder inflammation or bleeding and kidney/tubular injury
Low blood sodium and excessive water retention, which can cause confusion or seizures
Heart injury, lung inflammation or scarring, and severe liver blood-flow injury
Nausea, vomiting, mouth/bowel effects, hair loss, fatigue and impaired wound healing
Potentially permanent infertility, later cancers and pregnancy harm; allergic reactions

dactinomycin.name: Dactinomycin
dactinomycin.explanation: Dactinomycin binds to deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), the cell's genetic material, and disrupts production of ribonucleic acid (RNA), which carries instructions for cell activity. Cancer cells and healthy blood, mouth, gut and liver tissues can be affected.
visual: Medicine binds genetic material
Genetic instructions cannot be read normally
Blood, liver and infusion-site checks matter
dactinomycin.watch: Report fever, bleeding, severe mouth sores or diarrhoea, jaundice, increasing abdominal pain/swelling or rapid weight gain urgently. Tell staff immediately about infusion-site pain or burning. Report a new painful rash, especially in a previously irradiated area.
risks: Low blood counts, serious infection or sepsis, anaemia and bleeding
Mouth and gut ulceration, nausea, vomiting and bowel changes
Severe liver injury, including obstruction of blood flow through small liver vessels
Severe tissue damage if the medicine leaks outside the vein
Increased radiation effects or renewed inflammation in previously irradiated tissue, called radiation recall
Severe skin or allergic reactions, later cancers, fertility effects and pregnancy harm

irinotecan.name: Irinotecan
irinotecan.mechanism: Interferes with repair of genetic-material breaks
irinotecan.explanation: Irinotecan blocks topoisomerase I, an enzyme involved in handling deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), the cell's genetic material. Cancer-cell division is disrupted. Blood and bowel cells are also affected. Early infusion-related bowel symptoms and later diarrhoea need different treatment plans.
visual: Genetic-material repair is disrupted
Blood and bowel cells can be affected
Early and delayed diarrhoea need different actions
irinotecan.watch: Tell staff about cramping, sweating, runny eyes/nose or diarrhoea during or soon after infusion. Later watery stools require the prescribed diarrhoea plan and immediate oncology contact. Fever, dizziness, reduced urine, severe abdominal pain or inability to drink needs urgent assessment.
risks: Delayed diarrhoea that can be severe or life-threatening, causing dehydration, electrolyte loss or kidney injury
Early cholinergic symptoms such as sweating, abdominal cramps and diarrhoea during or shortly after infusion
Low blood counts, serious infection or sepsis, anaemia and bleeding; diarrhoea with low counts is especially hazardous
Nausea, vomiting, mouth soreness, appetite loss, fatigue and hair loss
Severe allergic reactions and uncommon serious lung inflammation
Fertility effects and pregnancy harm; medicine interactions can increase toxicity

temozolomide.name: Temozolomide
temozolomide.mechanism: Adds chemical damage to genetic material
temozolomide.explanation: The body converts temozolomide into an active substance that damages deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), the cell's genetic material, interrupting cell division. Although taken as capsules, it can cause serious blood, liver and infection problems and requires the prescribed checks.
visual: Capsules deliver active anticancer treatment
Genetic material is damaged
Blood, liver and infection checks continue
temozolomide.watch: Report fever, new cough or breathlessness, unusual bleeding, jaundice, severe rash or persistent vomiting urgently. Take capsules exactly as prescribed; do not replace a dose after vomiting. Follow the infection-prevention prescription and report any missed doses to the team.
risks: Low blood counts, serious infection or sepsis, anaemia and bleeding; prolonged marrow failure can occur
Opportunistic infections, including Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia, and reactivation of hepatitis B or other infections
Liver injury, including liver failure, which can occur after treatment has finished
Nausea, vomiting, appetite/bowel changes, fatigue, headache, rash and hair effects
Severe allergic or blistering skin reactions and lung inflammation
Later bone-marrow disorders or blood cancers, fertility effects and pregnancy harm

general: These reusable agent sections do not decide dose, phase, eligibility, prophylaxis or treatment duration. The parent author supplies current NCCP regimen sources and schedule-specific instructions.
No adverse-event percentages are invented or transferred from another cancer population. Generic risks must remain alongside all selected agent sections.
Clinical source hash freeze remains pending. No independent clinical/pharmacy approval, original-PDF binary verification or fresh visual-table review is claimed.
Contraception and breastfeeding instructions must be reconciled across every selected agent and the actual supplied products; do not use the older generic six-month interval as a universal rule.
dactinomycin: Current detailed safety source is the UK manufacturer SmPC, text revision 3 September 2025, EMC update 16 September 2025. It is not proof of current Irish product authorisation or supply.

Historical Irish PA1301/003/001 listing, https://www.hpra.ie/find-a-medicine/for-human-use/authorised-medicines/details/26050, records withdrawal on 1 April 2012 while also displaying Marketed. The old 2011 linked SmPC must not be labelled current Irish information.
This historical licence status does not mean the current NCCP regimen has been withdrawn. Pharmacy must confirm the supplied product and the applicable authorisation/unlicensed-supply arrangements.

UK product advice gives contraception during treatment and at least seven months afterwards for women/four months for men; no breastfeeding. These are agent-specific facts, not an automatically final combined-regimen interval.
cyclophosphamide: Current Irish source is explicitly Cyclophosphamide Seacross 500 mg, revision 7 January 2026; do not silently call it Endoxana or use the older UK Baxter 2016 text as current Irish evidence.
Ewing sarcoma is among the product indications; this does not establish that every tumour or combination in the NCCP source is licensed.
Product renal advice differs from NCCP IE/VAC. No numeric product dose adjustment is imported into patient definitions.
This product states contraception for six months after treatment for women/three months for men; breastfeeding is contraindicated. Reconcile all selected medicines.
vincristine: Current Irish product revision August 2026 specifies female contraception during and at least seven months after treatment; male contraception during and at least four months afterwards; breastfeeding avoidance during and for one month afterwards. Apply the reconciled combined-regimen plan.
CYP3A4/azole interactions can amplify neurotoxicity. The regimen's constipation and interaction plan must accompany the nerve-risk section.
Do not equate vincristine's blood-count effects with the principal marrow toxicity of the whole combination or copy incidence from other combinations.
doxorubicin: The retained HPRA example product was listed as authorised but not marketed when checked; confirm the actual supplied formulation. Conventional doxorubicin must not be substituted with a liposomal formulation.
Temporary red colour does not justify dismissing haematuria in an ifosfamide/cyclophosphamide combination. Lifetime exposure and regimen-specific ceilings remain professional planning issues.
irinotecan: Current October 2025 HPRA retained text supports delayed diarrhoea, weekly blood counts and liver monitoring. A fresh focused fetch was inaccessible; older Irish product text is explicitly supplementary for cholinergic/lung warnings, not dosing.

Early cholinergic symptoms and delayed diarrhoea are separate. Atropine glaucoma precautions and the prescribed loperamide/escalation plan belong in regimen support; no adult self-dosing schedule is supplied here.
Do not import colorectal doses, paediatric eligibility or numerical adverse-event rates into the sarcoma combinations.
temozolomide: EMA index lists product information updated 18 August 2026. One direct PDF attempt returned HTTP 429; no identical retry was made. Indexed official safety sections and readable manufacturer text were used; full latest-table inspection is not claimed.
Do not transfer glioma/radiotherapy seizure or neurological event rates, glioma dosing, or a 42-day radiotherapy monitoring calendar to these sarcoma regimens.
The NCCP 00504 and 00757 sources themselves require Pneumocystis prophylaxis: this is not an extrapolated requirement based only on the brain-radiotherapy product schedule.
The current product recommends liver tests after each cycle and warns of delayed hepatotoxicity. Baseline-only or pre-cycle-only wording would be incomplete.

00675: Keep the two-week adolescent/young-adult source context and 14-administration programme distinct from 00747.

Include ifosfamide/etoposide in odd administrations; vincristine/cyclophosphamide in the specified even administrations; doxorubicin only in administrations 2/4/6/8/10; dactinomycin in 12/14 only if selected by the consultant.
Discuss mesna/hydration limits, required growth-factor support, fertility, later cancers, daily neurological/urine checks and interactions. Actual support clocks remain with the schedule author.
00747: Preserve the adult three-week source context and its own recovery/support timing; do not copy 00675's exact growth-factor days.
Use the same named-agent selection safeguards as 00675; do not expand VAC automatically into a different drug combination.
Radiotherapy can change doxorubicin/dactinomycin delivery; the selected plan and associated radiation-related toxicity must be explained.
00504: Keep the full generic section plus irinotecan and temozolomide sections; do not omit oral-drug marrow/liver risks.
Explicitly disclose the unlicensed irinotecan/temozolomide indication in Ireland and follow local consent/Drugs and Therapeutics Committee policy.
Include delayed-diarrhoea action plan, infection prophylaxis, hepatitis-B screening/management, capsule precautions and no replacement after vomiting.
00754: Retain ifosfamide, vincristine and dactinomycin sections throughout their prescribed course; doxorubicin is present only in cycles 1–4.
Do not omit dactinomycin liver blood-flow injury, radiation recall or extravasation from generic chemotherapy consent.
Use the current source's three distinct phase charts and its own mesna/neurotoxicity rules; no automatic transfer of IE/VAC restart rules.
00757: Include all three named sections: vincristine bowel/nerve toxicity is additional to the irinotecan/temozolomide risks.
Explicit unlicensed-indication consent is required. Adult service scope versus the broader PDF age range remains a professional reconciliation, not permission to create paediatric instructions.

Discuss conditional temozolomide escalation as a clinician decision, required infection prophylaxis and competing diarrhoea/constipation risks without telling patients to self-adjust support medicines.
